title: The sine and cosine rules
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point teaches both the sine rule and the cosine rule, but the bank has them only as separate points, and neither one alone covers the whole brief, so a new point is safer than a partial match.

draft.title: The sine and cosine rules
card: a/sin A = b/sin B. Use it when you know a side and the angle opposite it, plus one more side or angle. Example: A = 30°, B = 45°, a = 8 gives b = 8 × sin 45° ÷ sin 30° ≈ 11.3.
c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C. Use it when you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.
These rules work in triangles with no right angle. Pythagoras and the basic ratios need a right angle.

If you know two sides and an angle that is not between them, the sine rule gives sin B. Both B and 180° − B have that sine, so there may be two triangles. Check that each one has angles adding to less than 180°.
draft.remember: Sine rule for opposite pairs. Cosine rule for two sides and the angle between, or three sides.

a.q: A triangle has sides of 7 cm and 9 cm with a 50° angle between them. Which rule finds the third side?
a.why: Two sides and the angle between them are known, so the cosine rule applies. The sine rule needs a side and its opposite angle, and neither is known here.
a.clue: Is there a side and angle that sit opposite each other?

b.q: In triangle ABC, A = 30°, a = 5 m and b = 8 m. Using the sine rule, sin B = 0.8. Which are the possible sizes of angle B?
b.why: sin B = 0.8 gives B = 53.1°, and the second angle is 180° − 53.1° = 126.9°. Both fit with 30°, as 30° + 126.9° is less than 180°. The value 36.9° is 90° − 53.1°, which is not the other angle with that sine.
b.clue: Two angles between 0° and 180° share the same sine.

check.summary: No problems found. The worked example (b ≈ 11.3) and both answers are correct: sin B = 8 sin 30° ÷ 5 = 0.8, giving B = 53.1° or 126.9°, and both are valid with A = 30°.
